Mind you I haven't ridden since I was little, I am a new customer, with a lifetime ahead to sell me gear, parts, services, etc...

I arrive at the local bike shop, a few minutes from where I live now, and start browsing the aisles. I am completely ignored for a good 10 to 15 minutes, until a small fat walks up and asks if he can help me. "Yes I am looking at bikes, and have a little bit of an idea lf what I am looking for."

"What are you looking at?"

"Start with the Muirwood 29?"

"You mean the 700? Cause the Muirwood we have is right here (right in front of me) and it is small for you. We have this instead, it is the same, but no disk breaks."

I asked about the breaks, he just says "rim breaks, im going to be in the store if you need anything"

Before using REI, you might try asking around for another suggestion of another LBS. Try cycling clubs in your area - you could end up with a decent bike, very poorly assembled at somewhere like REI.

If you're going online, you could try and find a used bike. I bought mine from a guy that buys one every winter so he doesn't get too much water on his racing bike and then sells it in spring. It was nearly new and paid about half price.

I'd check my local forums if I was looking for a bike.

There's lots of nice bike shops around me that I wouldn't even know were there if people didn't ask.
